# Trigonometry

## Core ideas and reasoning

In a right-angled triangle, identify the hypotenuse opposite the right angle and label opposite and adjacent relative to the chosen acute angle. Then sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent. Choose the ratio that connects the known and required quantities. Use inverse functions for angles, setting a calculator to degrees for degree questions. For a general triangle use the sine rule a/sin A = b/sin B when an opposite pair is known, or cosine rule a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A when given two sides and their included angle. Area = 1/2 ab sin C with included angle C. Bearings are measured clockwise from north using three digits. Sketch north lines and convert bearings into internal triangle angles before calculating. Trigonometric equations can have several solutions over an interval; use quadrants and reference angles. Do not round intermediate lengths or angles. Check that the hypotenuse is largest, angles sum to 180°, and units match the quantity asked.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

A right triangle has opposite side 6 cm and adjacent side 8 cm relative to θ. Find tan θ and θ to 1 decimal place.

tan θ = 6/8 = 0.75. θ = tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9°. Hypotenuse is 10 cm, so sin θ = 0.6 gives the same angle.

### Example 2

Find the third side of a triangle with sides 5 cm and 7 cm enclosing 60°.

c² = 25 + 49 - 2(5)(7)cos 60° = 39. c = √39 ≈ 6.24 cm. It lies between 7 - 5 = 2 cm and 12 cm as required.

### Example 3

Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm and 6 cm enclosing 30°.

Area = 1/2 × 8 × 6 × sin 30° = 12 cm². Independent check: height to the 8 cm base is 6 sin 30° = 3 cm; half base × height = 12 cm².

### Example 4

Solve sin θ = 1/2 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.

Reference angle is 30°. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II, so θ = 30° or 150°. No other solutions in the stated interval.

## Check your reasoning

Explain why the method applies before calculating or naming a result. Compare with a contrasting case. For calculations carry units, keep intermediate precision, then check by substitution, conservation or a second route. Describe observations separately from their explanation.
